messages:
sarah: Noticed a spike in 'compat-mode' traffic today after the soft-rewrite landed. A few tenants show >20% of requests being labeled compat even though clients requested v2.
lee: Is the router emitting a separate compat event or rewriting the model tag? Which metric drives billing?
sarah: Router currently emits `request.native` then `request.compat` when it rewrites for feature parity. Billing consumes any `request.*` metric. That causes inflated counts.
devin: We intentionally emitted both to preserve fidelity for debugging. But billing pipeline needs a reconciliation step. Otherwise tenants see surprise charges.
nash: (ops) We could add a `x-charge-source` header that the router sets to `primary` or `compat` and have billing prefer `primary` when present. That keeps the debug event but avoids double charge.
sarah: Agrees. Also we should track `compat_reason` (e.g., header, seq-len, model-mismatch) to understand why rewrites happen.
lee: For console UX: add a single-line indicator on the route page: "compat rewrites: 12% (last 24h)" and a breakdown by reason. Also provide a simulated impact tool so customers can see how billing would differ if we dedupe.
devin: Implementation note: router will continue to emit both events for now. Billing change: prefer `x-charge-source: primary` if present; if absent, fall back to current logic.
ops-bot: warning: changing billing preference is a breaking change for historical joins. Dashboards that sum `request.*` will need an annotated migration or new metrics. Backfill strategy required if we want historical parity.
sarah: Proposed rollout plan:
1) Add `x-charge-source` header and `compat_reason` metadata to router (v2.4).
2) Add `billing_preference=prefer_primary` flag in billing ingest (shadow mode for 72h).
3) Populate new console panels and simulation tool.
4) If metrics align, flip default and schedule backfill + dashboards migration.
lee: Can we sketch the simulation? Use last 7d data to compute `deduped_charge = sum(request.native) + sum(request.compat with x-charge-source=compat and no primary)` then compare to current. Quick query I used:
```
sum(request.native) by tenant
sum(request.compat) by tenant
# deduped = sum(request.native) + max(0, sum(request.compat)-sum(request.native)) ???
```
We need a deterministic dedupe rule.
devin: Dedupe rule idea: treat `request.native` as canonical. Any `request.compat` with identical request_id should be ignored for billing. If ids differ, prefer primary-like header. Need router to stitch IDs.
nash: Stitching IDs is doable but requires tinfo header propagation to downstream services. It's not free. Ops estimates ~2 engineer-weeks to make reliable.
sarah: For canary: enable `billing_preference` in shadow mode for 5 tenants for 3 days. Surface a new alert: `billing_differential_pct > 1%` on those tenants.
deploy-bot: started canary: billing-ingest v2-canary to us-east for tenants [t-178, t-209, t-312]. Health checks green.
lee: One more UX ask: when we flip default, show customers a banner: "We will dedupe compat rewrite events for billing starting DATE. Preview your estimated change" with a link to the simulator.
devin: Agreed. Also add an API endpoint for customers to fetch their 7d simulation JSON (so CS can triage).
ops-bot: note: don't forget audit logs for charge decisions. Finance will request immutable records for any deduped charge.
sarah: I'll draft the RFC with header names, billing logic pseudocode, console mockups, and the canary cadence. Posting in #eng-platform/rfc later today. Please review.
lee: I'll add the console mock for the route page and the simulator endpoint contract.
devin: I'll scope router changes and estimate. If we can do ID stitching cheaply we get clean billing reconciliation. If not, header preference path still fixes double-counting.
sarah: Thanks all. Quick action items: lee -> console mock, devin -> router estimate, ash -> bill ingest shadow flag, ops -> backfill impact assessment.
